root_cause_model.evidence: ZHI-138 is the issue ID and kd-phase0-digest-spec is the real upstream workflow task; the system cannot hold both at once
root_cause_model.blast_radius: every stage result, decision-log, spec, plan, and review is keyed by the wrong or ambiguous identity

root_cause_model.blast_radius: records can be written to and read from the wrong project silently; verify-code fails loud only after the damage is done

root_cause_model.cause: distributed path authority: stages, journal, route, review, and close each resolve paths independently
root_cause_model.evidence: helpers and writers re-call parser; CLI lacks a single --task-tracking-root

minimal_invariants: one workflow execution from make-decision through verify-code maps to exactly one immutable Run directory identified by an opaque run ID
every artifact, log, review, journal entry, and stage result is read from or written under that explicit Run directory, never inferred from cwd/git/env/config
external issue IDs are metadata in run.json and must never be path components
worktree_root is an absolute path stored in run.json at creation and never re-derived
a stage reads its previous stage result from the same Run directory unless given an explicit, read-only from_result path
all path access is mediated by a single Run module; no stage or helper may import a parser or resolver

alternatives.name: Minimal Run Model
alternatives.model: A workflow execution is a single Run directory with immutable run.json (run_id, target_repo, worktree_root, issue_ids[], status). Stages take --run-dir only. Previous results default to the same run; cross-run reuse uses --from-result <absolute-path> read-only. All artifacts live in run_dir/artifacts/. One Run module owns every path operation. Issue IDs are metadata.
pros: eliminates identity collapse and bootstrap deadlock
cons: breaks existing CLI and env contracts
spec/plan default outside business repo may surprise users
alternatives.migration_cost: medium: rewrite stage entrypoints, add Run module, build legacy adapter, update fixtures
failure_modes: callers forget to pass run-dir and get a clear loud failure
users expect business-repo specs and must add an explicit export/commit step

alternatives.name: ADR 0003 Task-Centric Explicit Model
alternatives.model: Keep the existing Projects/<project>/tasks/<task>/ directory model but add explicit task_tracking_root, current/upstream dual resolver, structured upstream references, stage-result v2 identity, producer artifact locator, and a worktree-ownership handoff journal.
pros: explicit roots fix the parser bug
cons: adds many new concepts instead of removing them
handoff lifecycle and compatibility rules are long-term maintenance costs
does not eliminate distributed resolution; it formalizes it
alternatives.migration_cost: high: new schema, new resolvers, journal lifecycle, v2 migration, broader test surface
failure_modes: handoff journal grows complex edge cases
long-term dual-mode compatibility fossilizes old and new paths
locator indirection can still point to wrong producer

alternatives.name: Worktree-Embedded Model
alternatives.model: Move all workflow records into a .workflowhub/ directory inside the business worktree. The worktree itself is the run container; run.json sits at .workflowhub/run.json.
pros: run location is obvious from the worktree
cons: violates the requirement that records live in the knowledge base
tool-nested worktree risks are inverted but not solved
alternatives.migration_cost: very high: changes storage contract and backup assumptions
failure_modes: nested tool repo still must distinguish business worktree from tool worktree

recommended_design.summary: Adopt the Minimal Run Model: one immutable Run directory per workflow execution, explicit --run-dir, single Run module, issue IDs as metadata, and a time-bounded legacy adapter.
recommended_design.authoritative_state: run.json at the root of an absolute run_dir. Required fields: run_id (opaque, immutable), created_at, target_repo, worktree_root (absolute), issue_ids[], status, stage_results{}. Optional: parent_run_id, from_results[]. Nothing else may infer project, task, or worktree.
recommended_design.stage_interface: workflowhub <stage> --run-dir <absolute-path> [--from-result <absolute-path>] [--issue-id <id>]. Environment fallback: WORKFLOWHUB_RUN_DIR only; no PROJECT_KEY, TASK_DIR, or cwd remote lookup. Each stage fails loud if run_dir is missing, run.json invalid, or required previous result absent.
recommended_design.path_resolution: A single Run module exposes openRun(runDir), artifact(relPath), previousResult(stage), publishResult(stage, data), worktreeRoot(), and lineage(). No other file may import a parser, resolver, or locator. Journal, review, route, and close all call this module.
recommended_design.lineage: Within a run, previous stage is implicit by convention. Cross-run reuse is explicit via --from-result and recorded read-only in run.json.from_results[]. There is no current/upstream task alias; issue IDs are metadata and workflow task IDs are run IDs.
recommended_design.worktree_lifecycle: make-decision creates run.json and records worktree_root. build-* stages operate in worktree_root but write all records to run_dir. verify-code reads only run_dir. close archives run_dir atomically and tags the worktree commit only if explicitly requested. A lightweight lock/session id in run.json prevents concurrent mutation.
recommended_design.failure_semantics: Fail loud and early. Missing --run-dir is an immediate error. Missing previous result stops the stage. Mismatched run.json schema/version stops execution. No search, no fallback, no heuristic matching. Errors name the exact expected path.

acceptance_tests: Nested tool repo: executing a stage from inside workflowhub nested in KnowledgeDigest with --run-dir pointing to KnowledgeDigest run resolves the correct run root without env vars
Dual identity: run ID workflow-kd-001 can carry issue_ids ["ZHI-138"] and upstream reference kd-phase0-digest-spec in metadata
Verify-code bootstrap: verify-code --run-dir /abs/run opens run.json and finds stage-result-build-code.json without cwd/env lookup
Missing run-dir failure: invoking any stage without --run-dir and without WORKFLOWHUB_RUN_DIR exits immediately with a clear error naming the missing argument
Single module enforcement: grep for resolveTaskRecordPaths, task-dir-parser, or worktree.json reads outside the Run module returns zero matches in stage/journal/review/route/close code
Cross-run read-only: --from-result /abs/other-run/stage-result-build-code.json is read-only and recorded in run.json.from_results[]
Legacy adapter: a legacy task dir converts to a Run dir with identical effective stage results, and invalid multi-path inputs are rejected
No remote fallback: no code path reads git remote origin of cwd to determine project identity

top_risks.risk: external callers and scripts invoke stage binaries without --run-dir
top_risks.mitigation: provide a loud error with an example command and a one-release deprecation of WORKFLOWHUB_TASK_DIR with a clear mapping to RUN_DIR

top_risks.risk: users expect spec/plan/tasks committed to the business repo by default
top_risks.mitigation: make close/export explicit: default workflow artifacts stay in run_dir, and --commit-to-worktree is an opt-in close flag
adapter is read-only and creates new Run dirs; legacy dirs remain until manual verification and sunset

top_risks.risk: concurrent stages or tools mutate the same worktree
top_risks.mitigation: run.json records session/lock; publish operations are atomic; close checks status invariant

top_risks.risk: nested repo topology still confuses human operators
top_risks.mitigation: all errors print absolute run_dir and absolute worktree_root; no relative or inferred paths in diagnostics

blocking_questions: Are there compliance or user expectations that require spec/plan/tasks to be version-controlled inside the business repository rather than kept as workflow artifacts?
Do any active integrations depend on the WORKFLOWHUB_TASK_DIR or WORKFLOWHUB_PROJECT_KEY environment variables in a way that cannot be replaced by RUN_DIR?
Can the team accept a breaking CLI contract change for the five stages within one release, or is a parallel entrypoint required?
Are there workflows where multiple concurrent runs legitimately share one worktree_root, or can we enforce one active run per worktree?
